segments.label: Natural Disasters & Extreme Weather
segments.script:
Today I want to walk you through three developments shaping how communities, parents, and policymakers are confronting extreme weather and climate-driven hazards.  
Time reports that Sesame Street has released a new episode focused on extreme weather, and the piece explores how climate and communication experts reacted to that choice. [REF:Time Magazine|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNbURkS1czOENtZThhRXNrcGVKZ2RDVmtYWDM4UzNpV1o1c0tCOERjQXhOVGotT25FdDFteTJqSkt0aFl2NzlQZmtBNUU3VlJING1rZmc4YTFkUlRtR2x1X3dGWDR1ZUM4MWJ2ZmpQR3IxTFZtTmJxS1RQWVBPR3NoS01tLTFHcjJQRXc?oc=5]  
Time situates the episode as part of a broader push to introduce young children to extreme weather risks while experts quoted in the article underscore the need to balance factual information with care for children’s emotional responses. [REF:Time Magazine|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNbURkS1czOENtZThhRXNrcGVKZ2RDVmtYWDM4UzNpV1o1c0tCOERjQXhOVGotT25FdDFteTJqSkt0aFl2NzlQZmtBNUU3VlJING1rZmc4YTFkUlRtR2x1X3dGWDR1ZUM4MWJ2ZmpQR3IxTFZtTmJxS1RQWVBPR3NoS01tLTFHcjJQRXc?oc=5]  
The Time reporting highlights that communication choices made in children’s media can influence how families perceive and respond to risk, a consideration that public-health and emergency managers should note when designing outreach. [REF:Time Magazine|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNbURkS1czOENtZThhRXNrcGVKZ2RDVmtYWDM4UzNpV1o1c0tCOERjQXhOVGotT25FdDFteTJqSkt0aFl2NzlQZmtBNUU3VlJING1rZmc4YTFkUlRtR2x1X3dGWDR1ZUM4MWJ2ZmpQR3IxTFZtTmJxS1RQWVBPR3NoS01tLTFHcjJQRXc?oc=5]  

At the same time, the World Health Organization has updated and maintained guidance on heat and health that is directly relevant to those same families and public officials. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  
WHO’s "Heat and health" material outlines that extreme heat poses significant, growing risks to health, and it provides practical recommendations about identifying vulnerable groups and implementing heat-health action plans. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  
That WHO guidance is material for local health departments and emergency planners who are already contending with hotter summers and more frequent heat extremes. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  

Finally, reporting in The Guardian outlines research that finds the climate crisis is "supercharging" the weather conditions that drive Europe’s wildfires, a phrase the article uses to characterize the scale and speed of change. [REF:The Guardian|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxONXRfVFVFa0tacm5WMGVKUHlLNk42bG9TRUdpdC16eXB0MHZfbmllYi1DT3BjLTBZMHdPbmlINGFIRUR3NUhOenR6NllXOFVPbnFHdC10SmpLTUNWSTJCTjRGS3VtdURRR1NLZ05xNjBKZEJVZ2pEb244Y1llQzhyUnA2Vlhja1JERGhFd0h5eEgwZndXYUdjM2xSZ0xpdDlpeUQwWjFUUTBhWER3ZmFvcTFKUXlIQQ?oc=5]  
The Guardian piece quotes researchers who describe hotter, drier conditions that increase fire weather risk across Europe and characterizes those findings as "extremely scary" for communities and responders. [REF:The Guardian|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxONXRfVFVFa0tacm5WMGVKUHlLNk42bG9TRUdpdC16eXB0MHZfbmllYi1DT3BjLTBZMHdPbmlINGFIRUR3NUhOenR6NllXOFVPbnFHdC10SmpLTUNWSTJCTjRGS3VtdURRR1NLZ05xNjBKZEJVZ2pEb244Y1llQzhyUnA2Vlhja1JERGhFd0h5eEgwZndXYUdjM2xSZ0xpdDlpeUQwWjFUUTBhWER3ZmFvcTFKUXlIQQ?oc=5]  
Taken together, these three items point to an urgent but practical set of priorities: how we talk about risk with children and families, how health systems prepare for heat, and how fire-prone regions must adapt to faster-moving seasonal extremes, conclusions that are reflected across Time, WHO, and The Guardian reporting. [REF:Time Magazine|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNbURkS1czOENtZThhRXNrcGVKZ2RDVmtYWDM4UzNpV1o1c0tCOERjQXhOVGotT25FdDFteTJqSkt0aFl2NzlQZmtBNUU3VlJING1rZmc4YTFkUlRtR2x1X3dGWDR1ZUM4MWJ2ZmpQR3IxTFZtTmJxS1RQWVBPR3NoS01tLTFHcjJQRXc?oc=5] [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5] [REF:The Guardian|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxONXRfVFVFa0tacm5WMGVKUHlLNk42bG9TRUdpdC16eXB0MHZfbmllYi1DT3BjLTBZMHdPbmlINGFIRUR3NUhOenR6NllXOFVPbnFHdC10SmpLTUNWSTJCTjRGS3VtdURRR1NLZ05xNjBKZEJVZ2pEb244Y1llQzhyUnA2Vlhja1JERGhFd0h5eEgwZndXYUdjM2xSZ0xpdDlpeUQwWjFUUTBhWER3ZmFvcTFKUXlIQQ?oc=5]

Beyond the media and public-health pieces we’ve already discussed, Climate Central’s mid-2026 update takes a close look at the U.S. tally of billion-dollar weather and climate disasters and places recent losses in that longer-term economic context. [REF:Climate Central|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihwFBVV95cUxPc1o2UkJ6Z1FIRkFubmNnQ2RlYkFGUWt0azFudkZnUnQ5cEw2SjVLYTJmbm5JR2pJUmo4TC1kS09ZLWY3NzJfbVlJSU5JSnY2NDh1dEhhTkZBalFpamlSSm13QkRfdzlkRGFwR0dENWVsUVc4Rl9tZDNScUdrQ25qbVliakNid2s?oc=5]  
That analysis draws attention to how the distribution of costly events and the sectors they hit can strain local recovery capacity and influence planning decisions at state and municipal levels. [REF:Climate Central|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihwFBVV95cUxPc1o2UkJ6Z1FIRkFubmNnQ2RlYkFGUWt0azFudkZnUnQ5cEw2SjVLYTJmbm5JR2pJUmo4TC1kS09ZLWY3NzJfbVlJSU5JSnY2NDh1dEhhTkZBalFpamlSSm13QkRfdzlkRGFwR0dENWVsUVc4Rl9tZDNScUdrQ25qbVliakNid2s?oc=5]  
For practitioners, that means mid-year economic snapshots can help prioritize where infrastructure hardening, flood mitigation, or evacuation planning will have the biggest payoff. [REF:Climate Central|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihwFBVV95cUxPc1o2UkJ6Z1FIRkFubmNnQ2RlYkFGUWt0azFudkZnUnQ5cEw2SjVLYTJmbm5JR2pJUmo4TC1kS09ZLWY3NzJfbVlJSU5JSnY2NDh1dEhhTkZBalFpamlSSm13QkRfdzlkRGFwR0dENWVsUVc4Rl9tZDNScUdrQ25qbVliakNid2s?oc=5]  

Turning back to WHO’s guidance, the agency supplies operational elements that jurisdictions can adopt, including early-warning triggers tied to specific health-sector responses and surveillance systems to detect heat-related illness in real time. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  
WHO also provides guidance aimed directly at protecting workers exposed to outdoor heat and at designing community cooling options that can be activated during extreme events. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  
And the WHO materials emphasize monitoring and evaluation so that health authorities can learn which interventions actually reduce morbidity and mortality as conditions and risks evolve. [REF:World Health Organization (WHO)|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPTkFYd3h0X3JaRjVZV0dMc0RXSjIwSlVyQVhyRkdHWTktSy1iSG14MVgzVzQ1akgtem9PcnpRSDN0dUJobF9QbXFNelZpamdZeVROazVUNDlFX3dBdnA2YnR1c3huTVlxR2NDbG9qUjgzNnk3QmJLa1BDdG5mNFB6dFJyMUd1QQ?oc=5]  

Putting these two bodies of reporting together offers a practical throughline: use economic and event-focused data to target investments and recovery planning, and adopt WHO’s operational tools to make sure those investments translate into measurable reductions in heat-related harm. segments.label: Space Exploration
segments.script:
Good morning, I’m bringing you two focused developments shaping lunar strategy and mission planning this week. [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5] [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] 

Encyclopedia Britannica has published a concise entry focused on Artemis III, noting the mission entry covers mission parameters, planned timing, crew assignment and the spacecraft to be used. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] Encyclopedia Britannica frames that entry as the current public reference for what Artemis III intends to accomplish and for how NASA is positioning the mission in its broader lunar campaign. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] That Britannica account synthesizes available information about the flight hardware and crew planning that observers have been tracking as NASA moves from lunar orbit operations toward surface sorties. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] For mission watchers, Britannica’s piece functions as a snapshot of NASA’s stated objectives and the spacecraft packages under consideration for an upcoming lunar return. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] 

Separately, Spaceflight Now reports a notable pivot by NASA and Northrop Grumman to repurpose elements originally intended for the Gateway as demonstrators for a Moon Base concept. [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5] Spaceflight Now’s reporting describes how program managers are looking to leverage existing Gateway hardware designs to accelerate demonstrations that would inform a sustained lunar base effort. [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5] The Spaceflight Now article lays out that the repurposing is a deliberate use of proven designs to reduce development time for surface demonstration systems. [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5] Taken together, Encyclopedia Britannica’s briefing on Artemis III and Spaceflight Now’s coverage of Gateway element repurposing signal a practical continuity in U.S. lunar planning from crewed sortie architecture toward infrastructure demonstrations. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5] 

I’ll be watching how NASA’s crewed mission planning, as summarized by Britannica, intersects with the hardware reuse pathway described by Spaceflight Now, and I’ll bring you updates as reporters and agencies publish them. [REF:Encyclopedia Britannica|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiV0FVX3lxTE82STR2WmxkS1VYQUZ1SHlwRERRN09tVzZyZk1sT3luc1ZVcWNRYXdCelBrMlpoMVctb1FfZDRoZ1psZTVXaVpialNkWnByUGN0Q215UXZ4UQ?oc=5] [REF:Spaceflight Now|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSE11eDcxTUp5ZmtKdi12T19xVUozcmY1V3NNVkJkQnpjMWFQU2Y4cnNUYlZvOTlRNS12NVRKcXJVOUQxQ19weWNldjh5amRoRjJuLWp5azc5VXFRT09aaEFkSW9jWDlDRzExZ3lDRjE3UGRZWHlFZVpteU5jaTJWUm1iQmRFa1k0UmtBTlFKZnlXQ21Lc2EtY1k2Uy1MalJLd3h1and5UV9nSk9jLTZXWEZ5NVoyUQ?oc=5]

Also this week, the Sun Sentinel published its Space Coast launch schedule, laying out the manifest of upcoming activity at Cape Canaveral and neighboring pads. [REF:Sun Sentinel|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTFA3Szk1OXVWTF9UdXR2Y0tjYXkzVzZyYXJ6Unk2WUtsSS1WbDR2d2ZOeTdDNUNKR3QxMFFaaDRMQ1BFbzdSVWVTYVYxd2FrWHpvZklzSGR0akRJM3NYdy1SemdVblJlWERzY1JscGFqMjR1N0hQUU9sQy1R?oc=5]

segments.script:
Good morning, this is AI Legal Briefs with a two minute overview of key rulings shaping AI and copyright law. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOYjBLM01uX0dLclpkY041M29fZHdIbm52RmhrcUxBdEhxZ1dzeVlHY25tRVJYcGRIejJ5ZjZZOU9RYnhsaFdGX0dWdG9aRGxpRDE5QzItNFNqWm9RVDRheEYxaFVuRm54aXh3cmRNLTlLSEV1ZVZ5azgzMDNtUGR4dVNjQUp2b0R1eldwSTVqeFJXMmJZQWl2MkxMNzFGYkxKM3ZR?oc=5]  
A German court has ruled that AI music company Suno broke copyright rules in a case that challenged how the company used copyrighted music. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOYjBLM01uX0dLclpkY041M29fZHdIbm52RmhrcUxBdEhxZ1dzeVlHY25tRVJYcGRIejJ5ZjZZOU9RYnhsaFdGX0dWdG9aRGxpRDE5QzItNFNqWm9RVDRheEYxaFVuRm54aXh3cmRNLTlLSEV1ZVZ5azgzMDNtUGR4dVNjQUp2b0R1eldwSTVqeFJXMmJZQWl2MkxMNzFGYkxKM3ZR?oc=5]  
Both Reuters and Deutsche Welle reported the court’s decision and framed it as a finding that Suno had violated copyright protections in its commercial AI music offerings. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOYjBLM01uX0dLclpkY041M29fZHdIbm52RmhrcUxBdEhxZ1dzeVlHY25tRVJYcGRIejJ5ZjZZOU9RYnhsaFdGX0dWdG9aRGxpRDE5QzItNFNqWm9RVDRheEYxaFVuRm54aXh3cmRNLTlLSEV1ZVZ5azgzMDNtUGR4dVNjQUp2b0R1eldwSTVqeFJXMmJZQWl2MkxMNzFGYkxKM3ZR?oc=5] [REF:dw.com|https://news.google.?oc=5]  
Deadline also covered the ruling, reporting that the decision came in a lawsuit specifically challenging AI use of copyrighted music and that the court’s judgment was against Suno. [REF:Deadline|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMif0FVX3lxTE01d2RNMnJVMkVtSVpncndabWVEaDhvYlRNZXJDT1o2TjB6QndNeUlQTTVKMUxveXVFT1EzZG5Mb1FCWkIyakVpaVNMMnJVWmg3SEZkZ3JITVFrSkVhZkFMb1Bfc0ZsZVJlX01zWk1jTVpvU2RPLXBybUExeHdBaFE?oc=5]  
Those outlet reports together make clear that at least one European court has now enforced traditional copyright protections against an AI-driven music service. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOYjBLM01uX0dLclpkY041M29fZHdIbm52RmhrcUxBdEhxZ1dzeVlHY25tRVJYcGRIejJ5ZjZZOU9RYnhsaFdGX0dWdG9aRGxpRDE5QzItNFNqWm9RVDRheEYxaFVuRm54aXh3cmRNLTlLSEV1ZVZ5azgzMDNtUGR4dVNjQUp2b0R1eldwSTVqeFJXMmJZQWl2MkxMNzFGYkxKM3ZR?oc=5] [REF:dw.com|https://news.google.?oc=5]  
Meanwhile, in a separate and contrasting decision, a court in India has ruled that OpenAI did not violate copyright held by the news agency ANI. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxOUEJhdXAtQzZaamdQRFdzXzlSdDRwSGdwanc2SW1CSFpwZDYyOXBia0t2WDdPZzFuTzBzempwMHlISzlBWS1LbXZLNHM3cTZub2M2T0toTGZaNFB3NW5SLUxyVzl5bHJrNmFzNWxhQlkzLUJNMzZnTElfLXJZZUtNbHZWQlg5Z255MjYxM29NRWNDUFFnU2hPc19wbUZsMzdEN3FwMGtXQlRhc1N1MUJlczBEWU1TUEFYSWQ2RGRyelNhUTFFQ3VLdQ?oc=5]  
Reuters reported that the Indian ruling cleared OpenAI of copyright infringement claims brought by the ANI news agency. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxOUEJhdXAtQzZaamdQRFdzXzlSdDRwSGdwanc2SW1CSFpwZDYyOXBia0t2WDdPZzFuTzBzempwMHlISzlBWS1LbXZLNHM3cTZub2M2T0toTGZaNFB3NW5SLUxyVzl5bHJrNmFzNWxhQlkzLUJNMzZnTElfLXJZZUtNbHZWQlg5Z255MjYxM29NRWNDUFFnU2hPc19wbUZsMzdEN3FwMGtXQlRhc1N1MUJlczBEWU1TUEFYSWQ2RGRyelNhUTFFQ3VLdQ?oc=5]  
Taken together, the Reuters, DW and Deadline coverage shows divergent judicial outcomes across jurisdictions this summer, with Germany finding a violation in one music-focused case and India finding no violation in a news-related dispute involving OpenAI. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOYjBLM01uX0dLclpkY041M29fZHdIbm52RmhrcUxBdEhxZ1dzeVlHY25tRVJYcGRIejJ5ZjZZOU9RYnhsaFdGX0dWdG9aRGxpRDE5QzItNFNqWm9RVDRheEYxaFVuRm54aXh3cmRNLTlLSEV1ZVZ5azgzMDNtUGR4dVNjQUp2b0R1eldwSTVqeFJXMmJZQWl2MkxMNzFGYkxKM3ZR?oc=5] [REF:dw.com|https://news.google.?oc=5] [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxOUEJhdXAtQzZaamdQRFdzXzlSdDRwSGdwanc2SW1CSFpwZDYyOXBia0t2WDdPZzFuTzBzempwMHlISzlBWS1LbXZLNHM3cTZub2M2T0toTGZaNFB3NW5SLUxyVzl5bHJrNmFzNWxhQlkzLUJNMzZnTElfLXJZZUtNbHZWQlg5Z255MjYxM29NRWNDUFFnU2hPc19wbUZsMzdEN3FwMGtXQlRhc1N1MUJlczBEWU1TUEFYSWQ2RGRyelNhUTFFQ3VLdQ?oc=5]  
That’s the briefing for today; I’ll return with deeper analysis of what these rulings may mean for platform liability and content training strategies in future episodes. [REF:Deadline|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMif0FVX3lxTE01d2RNMnJVMkVtSVpncndabWVEaDhvYlRNZXJDT1o2TjB6QndNeUlQTTVKMUxveXVFT1EzZG5Mb1FCWkIyakVpaVNMMnJVWmg3SEZkZ3JITVFrSkVhZkFMb1Bfc0ZsZVJlX01zWk1jTVpvU2RPLXBybUExeHdBaFE?oc=5]

Beyond courtrooms, professional and policy communities are also weighing in on how AI tools should be governed in legal contexts, and The Law Society published reporting that frames these debates within government policy and lawtech regulation. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5]  
That coverage highlights a focus on policy instruments and regulatory frameworks that aim to bring AI applications within the ambit of established legal and professional standards. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5]  
In particular, The Law Society’s piece situates questions about accountability, transparency and the interplay between new technology and existing duties owed by legal professionals. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5]  
On the international front, Sixth Tone reported that Chinese authorities have circulated draft regulations expressly aimed at AI-related copyright infringement. [REF:Sixth Tone|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOQjI5aUotVDhmbXBRNV9qNmlRTlhNTjZHNk1qVDk3czNrMXVXUmNmVHE1S1JyWUd2NFlpWHVfYm1zbHZmNnc5emNZWDNjLUFZNEUyS3lfQ1lYTTA4QkpLMlFXTHE3cnhCV29JR2NGOUZEUERxX1l0T004ZFFaUXFTeDFHd2ZhQkpJZUV4QW05T3J1WmZVVkowNWw3dUtLbUU?oc=5]  
Sixth Tone’s reporting describes a regulatory text that targets how generative systems handle copyrighted works and contemplates obligations for platforms and creators to address infringement risks. [REF:Sixth Tone|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOQjI5aUotVDhmbXBRNV9qNmlRTlhNTjZHNk1qVDk3czNrMXVXUmNmVHE1S1JyWUd2NFlpWHVfYm1zbHZmNnc5emNZWDNjLUFZNEUyS3lfQ1lYTTA4QkpLMlFXTHE3cnhCV29JR2NGOUZEUERxX1l0T004ZFFaUXFTeDFHd2ZhQkpJZUV4QW05T3J1WmZVVkowNWw3dUtLbUU?oc=5]  
Taken alongside the Law Society coverage, the Sixth Tone piece suggests regulators are considering both sectoral guidance for legal services and broader copyright enforcement tools that address training data and output attribution. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5] [REF:Sixth Tone|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOQjI5aUotVDhmbXBRNV9qNmlRTlhNTjZHNk1qVDk3czNrMXVXUmNmVHE1S1JyWUd2NFlpWHVfYm1zbHZmNnc5emNZWDNjLUFZNEUyS3lfQ1lYTTA4QkpLMlFXTHE3cnhCV29JR2NGOUZEUERxX1l0T004ZFFaUXFTeDFHd2ZhQkpJZUV4QW05T3J1WmZVVkowNWw3dUtLbUU?oc=5]  
For practitioners and platform operators, those two strands of reporting underscore a growing need to document data provenance, manage licensing and consider how professional obligations intersect with technical design choices, a point underscored in The Law Society’s analysis. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5]  
And as Sixth Tone reports on the draft regulatory language under consideration, firms operating across borders should watch how statutory obligations evolve in major markets and what that means for compliance and contractual arrangements. [REF:Sixth Tone|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOQjI5aUotVDhmbXBRNV9qNmlRTlhNTjZHNk1qVDk3czNrMXVXUmNmVHE1S1JyWUd2NFlpWHVfYm1zbHZmNnc5emNZWDNjLUFZNEUyS3lfQ1lYTTA4QkpLMlFXTHE3cnhCV29JR2NGOUZEUERxX1l0T004ZFFaUXFTeDFHd2ZhQkpJZUV4QW05T3J1WmZVVkowNWw3dUtLbUU?oc=5]  
I’ll continue to monitor reporting from The Law Society and Sixth Tone for developments on policy texts and draft rules that may affect how legal and technology sectors handle copyrighted material in AI systems. [REF:The Law Society|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPQ2pZd1l3eGxpT3REbVNTOEhkMDBGSHlfbE5zaW9OMV9RNWxqSnlkQTZ5NFN5Ty1FMjZrRndYcTdYdVNDcXVrb1ROMi1UMnFnbjNnaTI3c01uVnNyVS1lamVROUFOczRtYUh5T1gwN0d1bmNsWXBhYThuRHpDdDBWcXJTMGdKNmRQam9zbg?oc=5] [REF:Sixth Tone|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOQjI5aUotVDhmbXBRNV9qNmlRTlhNTjZHNk1qVDk3czNrMXVXUmNmVHE1S1JyWUd2NFlpWHVfYm1zbHZmNnc5emNZWDNjLUFZNEUyS3lfQ1lYTTA4QkpLMlFXTHE3cnhCV29JR2NGOUZEUERxX1l0T004ZFFaUXFTeDFHd2ZhQkpJZUV4QW05T3J1WmZVVkowNWw3dUtLbUU?oc=5]

Separately, The Moscow Times reported on August 13 that Russian businesses are increasingly turning to Chinese AI models as demand for locally accessible solutions surges. Taken together, these two reports sketch a bifurcated market: Reuters telling us U.S. model makers believe there is a new opening, and The Moscow Times documenting that in at least one major market, demand is being met by Chinese suppliers. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxQTjdFeGZSYlRfS0Z2ajQwNkNMQm1vUDE2SFJiRkF2NlNMTnVMRjdDaWlSOG9BTDZhWXZ5R3M3MENRbGpBaUFrRVptYmxEbmstQXBhdEVIYmhYQUJSQmRONzcxTG9MVlhmOFRxc0Y5QUdKMF9wRkZvaS10VUc4WFNuWjNPdlE3YVV5cjRoNnUtZ3VvSnJWd3BpVWl6X1BFMUptNzBTNDBYTGNCLXhFLUZ4YkVFMHpRNFE] [REF:The Moscow Times|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxOVzU1cmJsUTZkZFp4QXBxeVhYZW9DZjktNHBvRGN5REhLWTBNMlFtMGNJcUFIN1hERm9VWExzeF8yZXVHd3ZKekYwSElmREQ0ME02OVNzVjR0cjVyMkdpVHM3MHJoRFNTV2k4UEVrX2N3YjgzTzloUVpBRmdCNzhmMWdacmxlSVdUd2FUM3otSXU0eFRCalo5ZF9nTGREOHd1c2lhMUZoR1lhcXlVLUFF] 

For executives and policy watchers, the immediate takeaway from Reuters is that U.S. firms see commercial levers they can pull, while The Moscow Times suggests that geopolitical and market access dynamics are already driving customers toward Chinese-built models. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxQTjdFeGZSYlRfS0Z2ajQwNkNMQm1vUDE2SFJiRkF2NlNMTnVMRjdDaWlSOG9BTDZhWXZ5R3M3MENRbGpBaUFrRVptYmxEbmstQXBhdEVIYmhYQUJSQmRONzcxTG9MVlhmOFRxc0Y5QUdKMF9wRkZvaS10VUc4WFNuWjNPdlE3YVV5cjRoNnUtZ3VvSnJWd3BpVWl6X1BFMUptNzBTNDBYTGNCLXhFLUZ4YkVFMHpRNFE] [REF:The Moscow Times|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxOVzU1cmJsUTZkZFp4QXBxeVhYZW9DZjktNHBvRGN5REhLWTBNMlFtMGNJcUFIN1hERm9VWExzeF8yZXVHd3ZKekYwSElmREQ0ME02OVNzVjR0cjVyMkdpVHM3MHJoRFNTV2k4UEVrX2N3YjgzTzloUVpBRmdCNzhmMWdacmxlSVdUd2FUM3otSXU0eFRCalo5ZF9nTGREOHd1c2lhMUZoR1lhcXlVLUFF] 

That dynamic will be important to watch over the coming months as U.S. providers decide whether to pursue rapid expansion, specialization for regulated sectors, or partnerships to counter already-deployed Chinese models in markets described by The Moscow Times. 

We’ll monitor follow-on reporting to see how American companies act on the opportunities Reuters flagged and whether Chinese models deepen their presence in Russia and elsewhere as The Moscow Times reported. Reuters’ newsletter goes into detail about the kinds of commercial moves being considered, including rethinking product packaging and go-to-market approaches to chase pockets of paying customers that remain, according to that reporting. [REF:Reuters|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxQTjdFeGZSYlRfS0Z2ajQwNkNMQm1vUDE2SFJiRkF2NlNMTnVMRjdDaWlSOG9BTDZhWXZ5R3M3MENRbGpBaUFrRVptYmxEbmstQXBhdEVIYmhYQUJSQmRONzcxTG9MVlhmOFRxc0Y5QUdKMF9wRkZvaS10VUc4WFNuWjNPdlE3YVV5cjRoNnUtZ3VvSnJWd3BpVWl6X1BFMUptNzBTNDBYTGNCLXhFLUZ4YkVFMHpRNFE]

The Moscow Times piece adds that for many buyers the calculus includes speed of deployment and the availability of vendor support inside the country, factors that are influencing procurement choices now, as the paper reported. [REF:The Moscow Times|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxOVzU1cmJsUTZkZFp4QXBxeVhYZW9DZjktNHBvRGN5REhLWTBNMlFtMGNJcUFIN1hERm9VWExzeF8yZXVHd3ZKekYwSElmREQ0ME02OVNzVjR0cjVyMkdpVHM3MHJoRFNTV2k4UEVrX2N3YjgzTzloUVpBRmdCNzhmMWdacmxlSVdUd2FUM3otSXU0eFRCalo5ZF9nTGREOHd1c2lhMUZoR1lhcXlVLUFF]

segments.label: American Political Briefs
segments.script:
Good morning, I’m speaking to you on August 14, 2026, with American Political Briefs, and we’re tracking an escalating fight over who controls American elections heading into the midterms. [REF:Center for American Progress|https://news.google.].  

The Center for American Progress has published a detailed warning that the Trump administration is actively interfering in the 2026 midterm elections in ways designed to entrench what the report calls an “imperial presidency.” [REF:Center for American Progress|https://news.google.].  

Their analysis lays out a range of executive moves and policy shifts, arguing these actions are intended to reshape oversight, centralize authority over election administration, and create leverage against state and local officials. [REF:Center for American Progress|https://news.google.].  

That report comes amid broader reporting in The Guardian that the administration’s broader campaign to seize or expand federal election powers has generated what their coverage calls “chaos” and significant pushback from states, courts, and election officials. [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxNdmozcnozLVBKRWxqSlNEb1FHeXUwb2lUdndBYWFVOGtqTjJZalZMaEdlX1gtbnhrWDdGOUkwR0kxY0VSOUkzVy03UzBZSUxTazMwTWNGMnFFakNOdmxUTHBkTW5rZUpsUTRVTTAtdU5TLTBzT3hCOGdHcVQ0a3V5Y0dMVnZTT3MzQmdZ].  

Guardian journalists document a series of federal proposals and moves that critics say would allow the executive branch to override settled administration of elections at the state and local level, and those reports show a coalition of secretaries of state, election administrators, and legal experts pushing back. [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxNdmozcnozLVBKRWxqSlNEb1FHeXUwb2lUdndBYWFVOGtqTjJZalZMaEdlX1gtbnhrWDdGOUkwR0kxY0VSOUkzVy03UzBZSUxTazMwTWNGMnFFakNOdmxUTHBkTW5rZUpsUTRVTTAtdU5TLTBzT3hCOGdHcVQ0a3V5Y0dMVnZTT3MzQmdZ].  

And that pushback is not only rhetorical: The Guardian has reported recent legal rebukes to similar efforts, including an appeals court decision that rejected a bid by the Trump campaign to curb mail‑in voting across 23 states. [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxQb1dzZ1lGcXBsWG1aUzN6cHI4WGpIQUFBQmNKaFBJbl8wRVUybWhidGhyLXFLOVFjVGpLS2ZpTWlzV3VDWXBUV3R2SGtjNTV4ZG80N0F1aDBsZlJtQWI5dWExQk1FcmRPOHdjY19nb3I2Rk11N0VoelJWYndzX1JtNThEcDJiaFNZZlE].  

That appeals court ruling, as The Guardian lays out, stopped a sweeping bid to limit mail‑in ballots and underscores that courts remain a critical check as the administration tests the boundaries of federal authority over elections. [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxQb1dzZ1lGcXBsWG1aUzN6cHI4WGpIQUFBQmNKaFBJbl8wRVUybWhidGhyLXFLOVFjVGpLS2ZpTWlzV3VDWXBUV3R2SGtjNTV4ZG80N0F1aDBsZlJtQWI5dWExQk1FcmRPOHdjY19nb3I2Rk11N0VoelJWYndzX1JtNThEcDJiaFNZZlE].  

Taken together, these pieces paint a picture of a federal play for greater control over how elections are run that is meeting organized resistance in state capitals and in the courts, a dynamic that will shape the legal and political terrain as voters head to the polls this fall. [REF:Center for American Progress|https://news.google.] [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxNdmozcnozLVBKRWxqSlNEb1FHeXUwb2lUdndBYWFVOGtqTjJZalZMaEdlX1gtbnhrWDdGOUkwR0kxY0VSOUkzVy03UzBZSUxTazMwTWNGMnFFakNOdmxUTHBkTW5rZUpsUTRVTTAtdU5TLTBzT3hCOGdHcVQ0a3V5Y0dMVnZTT3MzQmdZ] [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxQb1dzZ1lGcXBsWG1aUzN6cHI4WGpIQUFBQmNKaFBJbl8wRVUybWhidGhyLXFLOVFjVGpLS2ZpTWlzV3VDWXBUV3R2SGtjNTV4ZG80N0F1aDBsZlJtQWI5dWExQk1FcmRPOHdjY19nb3I2Rk11N0VoelJWYndzX1JtNThEcDJiaFNZZlE].  

We’ll keep watching how federal initiatives, state defenses, and court decisions interact as the calendar moves toward November, and we’ll have updates as those fights produce new rulings, regulations, or election‑day consequences. [REF:theguardian.com|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxNdmozcnozLVBKRWxqSlNEb1FHeXUwb2lUdndBYWFVOGtqTjJZalZMaEdlX1gtbnhrWDdGOUkwR0kxY0VSOUkzVy03UzBZSUxTazMwTWNGMnFFakNOdmxUTHBkTW5rZUpsUTRVTTAtdU5TLTBzT3hCOGdHcVQ0a3V5Y0dMVnZTT3MzQmdZ]

Beyond the national headlines, regional reporting is tracking tightly contested local contests, including a special primary in Alabama for a U.S. House seat for which The Washington Post is running live results. [REF:The Washington Post|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxPQzk5aXh3OXRPUXlxY3EtQXZiQ2pVQ0Y0eGtjbWlWT3AwYTk5WWx0X1FOT2xCcEhXVnFscXpkUHUxQk9SNXh6a2xvMmhIVERNTlVRdnJURE9sLVV0cktGX21keVR3UXZPdWd2SldZMzFlTUk4cEY2Yjc5d1NJZ2xEd3V6Y0phcDVuVjVpZWxxaEZxMUVZTEQwZmZUZTdfbWJmdHc2bElmVGdaSkJNQzh3X0lrVWJiMlU4SHA3QW1qQ1RiX1E]  
That live page is presenting running vote tallies and frequent updates as counting continues across precincts in the Alabama contest, and readers can watch shifts in returns in near real time. [REF:The Washington Post|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxPQzk5aXh3OXRPUXlxY3EtQXZiQ2pVQ0Y0eGtjbWlWT3AwYTk5WWx0X1FOT2xCcEhXVnFscXpkUHUxQk9SNXh6a2xvMmhIVERNTlVRdnJURE9sLVV0cktGX21keVR3UXZPdWd2SldZMzFlTUk4cEY2Yjc5d1NJZ2xEd3V6Y0phcDVuVjVpZWxxaEZxMUVZTEQwZmZUZTdfbWJmdHc2bElmVGdaSkJNQzh3X0lrVWJiMlU4SHA3QW1qQ1RiX1E]  
In a different part of the country, VPM has published a detailed guide to who is appearing on the ballot for Central Virginia’s congressional seats, giving voters a clear rundown of the names and matchups they will encounter. [REF:VPM|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxQODlEc2dhNmJEOE9rd2tpOVdyY1BnZHVBXzRnSnVMdEZiUmpuak0tSjBkOFd5Tm9CN29XNTg5dlpqWC1yME43Ym1nNWZteUdjeTRqbXdJajFIQU1NeWdibDZGWGZrZmFXZEN1U0RxM1pZX1ljcEJOaFJ6ZHB1NXM0X3cwWkJ3NlAtdDNxbmZVakNPaVh3dmdFb2dvemlQY3JCdEhB]  
That VPM package walks through district by district so local voters, campaign staff, and observers can quickly identify the ballot choices in several competitive congressional fights. [REF:VPM|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxQODlEc2dhNmJEOE9rd2tpOVdyY1BnZHVBXzRnSnVMdEZiUmpuak0tSjBkOFd5Tm9CN29XNTg5dlpqWC1yME43Ym1nNWZteUdjeTRqbXdJajFIQU1NeWdibDZGWGZrZmFXZEN1U0RxM1pZX1ljcEJOaFJ6ZHB1NXM0X3cwWkJ3NlAtdDNxbmZVakNPaVh3dmdFb2dvemlQY3JCdEhB]  
Separately, News4JAX is focusing attention on voting access and local concerns about election administration, reporting on the anxieties, advocacy, and policy debates playing out in communities ahead of high‑visibility contests. [REF:News4JAX|https://news.google.]  
That News4JAX reporting emphasizes the local voices — from advocacy groups to administrators — who are shaping conversations about access, security, and the practical mechanics of voting in their communities. [REF:News4JAX|https://news.google.]  
Taken together, The Washington Post’s live vote page, VPM’s ballot guide, and News4JAX’s community‑level reporting offer three different windows into how local races, candidate lists, and voter‑access concerns are unfolding on the ground. [REF:The Washington Post|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxPQzk5aXh3OXRPUXlxY3EtQXZiQ2pVQ0Y0eGtjbWlWT3AwYTk5WWx0X1FOT2xCcEhXVnFscXpkUHUxQk9SNXh6a2xvMmhIVERNTlVRdnJURE9sLVV0cktGX21keVR3UXZPdWd2SldZMzFlTUk4cEY2Yjc5d1NJZ2xEd3V6Y0phcDVuVjVpZWxxaEZxMUVZTEQwZmZUZTdfbWJmdHc2bElmVGdaSkJNQzh3X0lrVWJiMlU4SHA3QW1qQ1RiX1E][REF:VPM|https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxQODlEc2dhNmJEOE9rd2tpOVdyY1BnZHVBXzRnSnVMdEZiUmpuak0tSjBkOFd5Tm9CN29XNTg5dlpqWC1yME43Ym1nNWZteUdjeTRqbXdJajFIQU1NeWdibDZGWGZrZmFXZEN1U0RxM1pZX1ljcEJOaFJ6ZHB1NXM0X3cwWkJ3NlAtdDNxbmZVakNPaVh3dmdFb2dvemlQY3JCdEhB][REF:News4JAX|https://news.google.]  
I’ll keep an eye on those three reporting tracks and bring you any significant shifts in returns, candidate developments, or local reporting about access that those outlets surface.
